subject: Decision Making
title: When to Decide Alone
description: One-minute skill: When to Decide Alone.

hook.text: Not every decision needs a group. Sometimes one person with clear authority makes better, faster, and cheaper choices.

buildup.text: Routine decisions, reversible choices, and time-critical calls are better made alone.

discovery.text: The key question: does this decision benefit from diverse information? If yes, use a group. If no, decide and move on.

twist.text: Many organizations default to group decisions to share blame. Committees exist for political cover, not better outcomes.

climax.text: Knowing when to decide alone is as valuable as knowing how to decide together. Match the method to the decision.

punchline.text: Need diverse info? Use a group. Need speed? Decide alone. Match method to need.

quiz.question: When is a solo decision better than a group decision?
options: For routine, reversible, or time-critical decisions that don't benefit from diverse input
